subject: C02
required_fixes: [P1] RF05 — Preserve the durable write-ahead barrier for Keychain effects. crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:584 converts StoreError::Unconfirmed into Ok(()); ConfigureScanCredential at :1051–1072 then starts the Keychain put even though the new record's cleanup entry was not confirmed durable. If the put lands and a crash restores the last confirmed document before a later confirmed save, that document contains neither the new credential index nor its cleanup entry. Core::start at :720 drains only ledgered records, leaving the secret untracked. The durability warning does not provide recovery ownership for that secret. Keep the truthful handling of already-visible metadata changes, but distinguish confirmed persistence when authorizing protected-storage effects, or supply another durable recovery mechanism. Acceptance: inject Unconfirmed at the credential write-ahead save, interrupt before a confirmed commit, restore the pre-save durable document while retaining the synthetic vault, and restart; no newly written secret may survive without durable indexing or cleanup ownership. Exercise replacement as well as first entry.
evidence_gaps: T06 still lacks the combined unconfirmed-save/credential-write/crash case. saves_are_refused_only_when_nothing_was_written tests tenant metadata and performs a confirmed save before restart; ScriptedStore preserves the latest visible document even for Unconfirmed. The new FileStore fault test verifies visibility after rename, but does not establish protected-record recovery when that unconfirmed replacement is lost. Add a production-interface regression for RF05 that distinguishes visible state from the last confirmed durable state, and bind fresh checks to the repaired source.
limitations: All four fingerprints, source inventory, packet references, tool executable hashes, run-log hashes and fixture executable/bundle hashes independently matched. Rechecked the C01 receipt, verdict and raw-output hashes, completion record and base-commit ancestry.

Inspected retained passing results: 48 frontend, 23 core, 40 context/transport, 12 IPC, 6 Keychain and 164 published-SDK tests; the 30 targeted frontend tests overlap the 48. Independently reran three existing in-memory fixture tests for held-write reset, partial purge/document-removal failure and unconfirmed metadata saves; all passed. Independently executed the production TypeScript parser in memory and confirmed the previously accepted missing-count case is now rejected. No compilation or full-suite rerun was performed.

The prior reset ordering, stale-context and partial-progress fixes are supported by source inspection and targeted tests. The prior post-rename refusal/memory rollback defect is corrected for visible metadata; RF05 concerns the remaining protected-write durability prerequisite.

RF05 follows from production control flow and the explicit Unconfirmed durability contract; no real filesystem failure or power-loss experiment was performed. No application files, product endpoints or credential stores were accessed for mutation; only designated review artifacts were written.

Native acceptance remains implementer-recorded fixture evidence with 12 passing checks, dedicated fixture Keychain and app-controlled lock. Production signed identity/upgrade behavior remains C26. System proxy changes were tested through environment variables, not changed macOS proxy settings; spoken VoiceOver and filesystem tracing were not recorded. C03 production Scan integration and C25 live qualification remain outside this review.
